newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-STARS CLASH IN BEST RACE FOR YEARS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-STARS CLASH IN BEST RACE FOR YEARS.

text.p: In one of the best races for years, French raider Helissio takes on two other globe-trotting superstars in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes at Ascot on Saturday.

Since October, the top three in the betting -- Helissio, Singspiel and Pilsudski -- boast between them victories in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, Japan Cup, World Cup, Breeders' Cup Turf, Coronation Cup and Eclipse Stakes.
Ascot racecourse director Douglas Erskine-Crum said: "The showdown between these horses has caught the imagination of the racing world."

No wonder backers have been licking their lips as they relish the eight-strong field which remarkably also features Royal Ascot winners Predappio and Kingfisher Mill and last year's St Leger scorer Shantou.

The fact that Shantou, who has won five of his six career starts, is on offer at 25-1 speaks volumes about the race, although Frankie Dettori switching from Shantou to Singspiel has also been a major factor in Shantou's derisory price.
Cash Asmussen finds himself on board Helissio (currently 6-4 favourite) after French champion Olivier Peslier was claimed for duties at home.
Asmussen, Texan-born but French-based for many years, said: "Despite the high-quality line-up, I am sure that if Helissio runs up to his best form then no one will beat him.
"The beauty of Helissio is that he is a flexible horse to ride and that means that one can adapt the tactics to fit the circumstances."
Helissio was one of the best Arc winners for years last October and, provided the ground is not too firm, he is the one they all have to beat,

Trainer Michael Stoute, providing the main opposition, has had a golden time with Japan and World Cup winner Singspiel (2-1) and Pilsudski (11-2), although the latter could be withdrawn if the ground became too firm.
Nick Cheyne, clerk of the course, said: "We will continue to monitor the weather situation and we will continue watering even on Friday night if necessary."

Backers have taken the hint about Breeders' Cup Turf and Eclipse winner Pilsudski, who has drifted in the betting, preferring instead Predappio (8-1) who gave top American Gary Stevens his first Royal Ascot win.
Stevens flies in for the mount again and Predappio is clearly improving although the Godolphin team, trained by champion Saeed bin Suroor, has not been in top form lately.

Swain (12-1), to be ridden by John Reid, rarely runs a bad race but as the second Godolphin runner, doubts must persist about the stable's form. Kingfisher Mill (14-1) was a brilliant Royal Asoct winner a month ago but faces a huge step-up in class.

Shantou (25-1) needs the Dettori magic to produce his very best but deputy Gary Hind is a more than capable rider, while 50-1 outsider Strategic Choice has earned his place in this famous line-up with several gutsy performances over the years at the very top level, including a third in the Japan Cup when dead-heating with Helissio.
